title: AWM: Answerable Working Memory for Long-Document VQA Agents

visual_explainer.question: After an agent reaches relevant pages, can terminal working memory still be a distinct evidence bottleneck that should be measured and optimized separately?
visual_explainer.takeaway: AWM measures whether the final source-linked working memory can answer the question after page images and trajectory context are removed, then adds that answerability signal to GRPO while keeping the retrieval/tool loop fixed.
visual_explainer.compared_with: The same Qwen3-VL-4B agent, RAG Top-3 harness, tools, memory schema, prompts, optimizer, and SFT checkpoint under answer-only GRPO; an EP-given setting additionally removes page-access differences.

analysis.tldr: AWM separates page access from evidence materialization by asking whether terminal working memory alone remains answerable. On MMLongBench-Doc, 42.5% of correct EP-given answers have unanswerable terminal memory. Against the same answer-only GRPO agent, AWM-GRPO improves final accuracy 51.6→53.9 on MMLongBench-Doc and 57.4→60.1 on LongDocURL; in the EP-given control it improves final/memory-only accuracy 45.4/41.2→48.0/43.5 and lowers memory-missing-correct 19.1%→16.4%.
analysis.problem: Evidence-page access and final-answer correctness can hide a separate failure: the agent observed the right source but failed to preserve question-relevant evidence in state that survives later context loss.
analysis.core_idea: Treat source-linked terminal working memory as an answer-supporting artifact. A frozen reader answers from only the question and terminal memory; a frozen scorer turns memory-only answerability plus final correctness into a GRPO reward that prefers answer-correct trajectories with usable memory.
analysis.agent_loop: query → retrieve top-3 page images → inspect → mandatory source-linked memory update → repeat up to 15 steps → final answer + terminal working memory
analysis.retrieval_design: The deployed agent keeps the same Jina-v4/Qdrant top-3 page retrieval interface across controlled AWM variants. The intervention changes how the policy is rewarded for what it commits after retrieval, not the retrieval backend or answer prompt.
compared_to: same SFT checkpoint with answer-only GRPO
VLM + RAG Top-3 without terminal working memory
EP-given answer-only GRPO with gold evidence pages
analysis.evidence: The strongest attribution is the same-family AWM-GRPO versus answer-only GRPO comparison: 51.6→53.9 and 57.4→60.1 final accuracy on the two benchmarks. With retrieval replaced by gold evidence pages, final accuracy 45.4→48.0, memory-only accuracy 41.2→43.5, and Pmmc 19.1%→16.4%, isolating memory extraction from page access.
analysis.why_it_matters: It exposes evidence materialization as a causal control surface between retrieval and answering: reaching evidence, preserving it in agent state, and grounding that state are three separable properties and should not be collapsed into retrieval quality.
limitations: Controlled results cover one 4B policy and two long-document VQA benchmarks; transfer to larger models and other document distributions is untested.
Memory-only answerability depends on one frozen Qwen3-14B reader and the benchmark judge; it is not claim-level source-grounding verification.
AWM-GRPO adds two short Qwen3-14B text passes per rollout during training, so its matched inference loop does not imply matched training compute.
Per-source analysis is uneven: table and layout questions show worse Pmmc under AWM even when aggregate Pmmc improves.
